title: Lipschitz Bandits with Stochastic Delayed Feedback
claim: Our algorithms keep sublinear regret across reward shapes and delay distributions, with regret growing only mildly as average delay increases.
layout: 2x3 grid of line plots; rows vary delay type, columns vary reward function
description: A 2x3 grid of matplotlib line charts showing cumulative regret against time horizon, from 0 to 60000. Rows are delay types: the top row uses uniform (bounded) delay and the bottom row uses geometric (unbounded) delay. Columns are reward functions: triangle, sine and two-dimensional. Each panel has red, green and blue curves for no delay, E[tau]=20 and E[tau]=50. Solid lines are Delayed Zooming and dashed lines are DLPP. Every curve is concave and sublinear. Regret grows in order red, green, blue, so more delay means more regret. In the 1-D panels the dashed curves sit above the solid ones. In the 2-D panels the dashed curves sit below. Each panel has a title, a legend in the top left, and thick black axes borders.
caption: Plots of cumulative regrets of Delayed Zooming algorithm (solid line) and DLPP (dashed line) under different settings with three levels of average delay: no delay (red), E[τ] = 20 (green) and E[τ] = 50 (blue). The first row corresponds to uniform distribution for the bounded delays, and the second row corresponds to geometric distribution for the unbounded delays. The three columns correspond to the triangle, sine, and two-dimensional reward function (from left to right).
abstract: The Lipschitz bandit problem extends stochastic bandits to a continuous action set defined over a metric space, where the expected reward function satisfies a Lipschitz condition. In this work, we introduce a new problem of Lipschitz bandit in the presence of stochastic delayed feedback, where the rewards are not observed immediately but after a random delay. We consider both bounded and unbounded stochastic delays, and design algorithms that attain sublinear regret guarantees in each setting. For bounded delays, we propose a delay-aware zooming algorithm that retains the optimal performance of the delay-free setting up to an additional term that scales with the maximal delay $Ï_{\max}$. For unbounded delays, we propose a novel phased learning strategy that accumulates reliable feedback over carefully scheduled intervals, and establish a regret lower bound showing that our method is nearly optimal up to logarithmic factors. Finally, we present experimental results to demonstrate the efficiency of our algorithms under various delay scenarios.
